guide.summary: Private app on your own workspace (self-serve, wait none); Public app, unlisted, installed from your product (app review); Public app listed in the Intercom App Store (approval path unconfirmed). Where the path is unconfirmed, the agent did not find it in the provider's docs.
guide.verdict: Easiest: Private app on your own workspace (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app, unlisted, installed from your product (app review).

composio.note: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Intercom. For production, a custom app lets users see your app name instead of Composio.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes: Composio's managed app works. For production you will likely want your own app so users see your brand, you get dedicated quota, and you control scopes.
reasons: Consent screen shows 'Composio wants to access your account' with the managed app
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval
Default managed scopes may not match what you need

prerequisites.title: Developer Hub account and Intercom workspace
prerequisites.detail: You must follow Intercom's registration requirements, and using the Intercom Service itself requires the separate Customer Agreement.

prerequisites.title: Staging app for development
prerequisites.detail: Create a private staging app from the Developer Hub home page; the production app is labeled Public.

prerequisites.title: Test account or set-up instructions for the reviewer
prerequisites.detail: If your service needs an account or subscription, supply test credentials or instructions in the description.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config (prototype)
steps.detail: Use Composio's managed Intercom OAuth app for prototyping, via Composio's API.
steps.done_when: A connected account works with the managed app.

steps.title: Enable OAuth in Developer Hub
steps.detail: Tick 'Use OAuth' on the Authentication page, then add redirect URLs (HTTPS only). Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: OAuth is enabled and redirect URL saved.

steps.title: Draft minimal scope list
steps.detail: Pick only the scopes your agent needs; webhook topics need matching scopes. Over-privileged scopes are the top rejection reason.
steps.done_when: Each scope maps to a feature.

steps.title: Select scopes in Developer Hub
steps.detail: Tick the scope checkboxes on the Authorization page.

steps.title: Create auth config with your credentials
steps.detail: Create the Composio auth config with your client ID and secret from the Basic Information page.

steps.title: Prepare reviewer description and test access
steps.detail: Draft the app description, how it works with Intercom, and set-up instructions.

steps.title: Record end-to-end OAuth demo video
steps.detail: Show install, full functionality and uninstall, with full client_id and state in the OAuth URL. Showing too much is better than too little.

steps.title: Prepare listing, images and partner form
steps.detail: Fill out listing fields, 2-5 PNG images, icon, and partner form with company details.

steps.title: Submit app for review
steps.detail: Submit via the Test and publish section of the Developer Hub.
steps.done_when: Yellow banner shows app is in review.

steps.title: Wait for Intercom review
steps.detail: Review can take up to seven business days; resubmission after changes takes up to the same again.

traps.title: Over-privileged scopes cause rejection
traps.detail: This is the most common reason for initial rejection, and approval may grant fewer permissions than requested.

traps.title: Demo video must show full client_id and state
traps.detail: Missing OAuth steps or functionality force you to resubmit the video.

traps.title: Broken installation links reject the listing
traps.detail: Broken or unclear links in the Installation status section cause rejection and resubmission.

traps.title: Intercom name banned in app name and icon
traps.detail: An app name containing Intercom will not be approved; the icon cannot contain the Intercom logo.

traps.title: Approval can be revoked after the fact
traps.detail: Intercom may review apps and security policies at any time and revoke credentials if non-compliant.

traps.title: Each user can revoke access
traps.detail: Each end user must authorize the app and may revoke their token at any time.

blockers.symptom: Review is rejected or changes requested
blockers.what_it_means: Scopes, links or the demo video did not meet requirements.
blockers.what_to_do: Fix the issues, resubmit, and wait up to seven business days again.
blockers.agent_can_help: Audit scopes against features and check links before resubmitting.

blockers.symptom: No response from Intercom after the stated review window
blockers.what_it_means: A developer reported a submission unreviewed after 15 days (around 2021) with no support reply.
blockers.what_to_do: Escalate through the Intercom community forum.

open_questions: Is a review round typically shorter or longer than 7 business days today? Ask in the Intercom developer community or support.
Do customers' workspace admins need to approve installs? Docs only say the user approves permissions; confirm with a test install.
Is there a minimum customer or install count for App Store listing? Not found; check the App Partner Program page or ask Intercom.
